# Each tissue does its own job

<!-- STEP id="many-jobs" -->
## Many kinds of cells

A neem tree has cells that support it, cells that carry water, cells that carry food and cells in its leaves that make food. Each group of similar cells forms a tissue, and each tissue does its own job.

<!-- STEP id="division-of-labour" -->
## Sharing the work

This sharing of work between tissues is called **division of labour**. Because each tissue does its own job well, the whole body works better than it would if every cell had to do every job.

<!-- STEP id="few-divide" -->
## A few groups of cells keep dividing

Most cells in a grown tree have become specialised for their job, and they no longer divide. Yet the tree keeps growing, because it has a few small groups of cells that keep dividing and making new cells.

**A plant grows because a few groups of its cells keep dividing, while most of its cells do their own special jobs.**
